correctness.rationale: Complete definitions, finite parameters and exact assumptions are explicit. The Bernstein basis proves equivalence of conditional and independent-retention laws; exact binomial inversion recovers both degree multisets. Direct 16-subset calculation validates the two four-plant/four-pollinator witnesses with distinct four-cycle counts. Canonical complete search includes every possible distinct nonempty plant neighborhood combination, filters nonempty/distinct pollinator columns and connectivity, quotients all guild-respecting permutations, and compares full exact survivor histograms. Through seven vertices the 28 connected twinfree isomorphism classes have no profile collision, with first at eight. Bundled checker and independent deletion function reproduced complete exact certificate byte-for-byte. Nothing is inferred beyond finite-census range.

evidence: Memmott et al. use random primary pollinator extinction and declare plants extinct after losing all pollinators, with robustness curves for observed large ecological networks (methods and results, pp. 2606–2607).
Bane et al. compare robustness distributions across several knockout models and weighted interaction rules, not exact side-preserving topological identifiability under complete count profiles.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The sources include the mechanistic model and structural explanations but do not establish a stronger exact all-law graph-reconstruction theorem or the sharp eight-species failure. Their emphasis is forward robustness analysis instead of the present inverse problem.

evidence: The ecology papers define and analyze knockout robustness, generally as a mean curve, distribution of area-under-curve robustness values, or model comparison; those results do not imply a graph-reconstruction minimum.

The neighborhood-polynomial and neighborhood-hypergraph sources have distinct observables: respectively common-neighbor existence for subsets and full neighborhood incidence realization, not the complete count response without incidence labels.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The strongest plausible implication checked is that a fully observed neighborhood hypergraph recovers an incidence graph; losing correspondence between subsets and outputs invalidates that implication here. The eight-species witness retains both degree multisets and all count-distribution coefficients, while its cycle profile differs. No checked paper supplies the same statement as a corollary.

evidence: The same observation can be expressed as a bivariate subset-neighborhood-union-size polynomial; fixed-size conditional laws and independent retention laws are equivalent by the Bernstein basis, proved in RESULT.md.
Bergold, Hochstättler and Mayer count sets possessing at least one common neighbor, which does not record all sizes of unions of neighborhoods by input subset size.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: A statement in terms of unweighted neighborhood complexes, common-neighbor polynomials, or marginal degree lists is not automatically equivalent to the complete union-cardinality histogram. The exact witness has equal full histogram, not merely mean and variance; no inspected source proves the sharp smallest collision for this invariant.

evidence: An exact exhaustive independent class construction and comparison is packaged for all admissible network sizes up to eight; the witness profile is listed in RESULT.md.
Boros, Gurvich and Zverovich characterize neighborhood-hypergraph realizations in their abstract, which retains substantially richer incidence than the present marginal count distributions.

originality.rationale: Closest primary literature addresses random knockout ecological robustness (Memmott et al. 2004; Bane et al. 2018), common-neighbor polynomials (Bergold et al. 2022), and full neighborhood hypergraph realization (Boros et al. 2008). Their checked statements do not imply the complete unlabeled count-profile identification threshold, eight-species degree-matched obstruction, or both-degree recoverability theorem; queries included alternate polynomial and graph-reconstruction vocabulary and a published mathematical-record search. Inaccessible 2008 full text and potential equivalent hypergraph/coverage-polynomial results remain explicit residual risks.
residual_risks: The full 2008 Boros–Gurvich–Zverovich technical paper was inaccessible; only the publisher abstract could be checked.
A different graph-polynomial or hypergraph notation could already encode the sharp finite collision. Bibliographic novelty is best-knowledge, not externally certified.
Ecological model choice is deliberately idealized; the graph theorem is exact only in the stated binary one-way knockout setting.

value.rationale: The exact observation model is a standard ecologically motivated random knockout experiment, and the question asks which interaction structures complete count data can recover. The theorem determines the precise smallest connected twinfree ambiguity, supplies two networks with the same full response laws and both guild degree multisets yet distinct 4-cycle redundancy, and gives a general analytic recovery statement for both degree multisets. This is a sharp natural identifiability boundary and not an arbitrary graph slice, textbook deduction or low-order moment recomputation; no larger-order or empirical inference claims are made.
